summary.headline: Seamec Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 58% YoY to Rs330 crore and PAT more than doubled to Rs103 crore; FY27 growth guided at about 15%.
summary.overview: Management reported record FY26 revenue and profitability, with consolidated revenue of Rs1,000 crore (up 47%) and PAT of Rs253 crore versus Rs88 crore. Q4 consolidated EBITDA reached Rs162 crore versus Rs91 crore a year earlier. Management guided FY27 revenue and profit growth of about 15% and a stable EBITDA margin of 40-42%, while flagging that vessel Seamec Paladin remains stuck in Dubai due to the West Asia conflict, which removes its revenue for April-May. The company added two ONGC O&M contracts with Supreme Hydro and SEAMEC AGASTYA, and is acquiring SEAMEC ANANT (about $70 million capex in FY27).

segments.name: Offshore vessel charter (DSV/MSV/OSV fleet)
segments.commentary: Management says fleet utilisation is almost 100% excluding off-hire from dry dock, breakdowns and seasonality. Diamond (OSV) on ONGC charter earns about $8,750/day per Vinay Agarwal; renewal expected at 10-15% higher.

segments.name: International (Saudi Arabia, Dubai)
segments.commentary: International markets contribute about 10-15% of revenue. Dubai operations have been pruned; one vessel is working for Saudi Aramco and one vessel (Paladin) is stuck in Dubai dry dock.

segments.name: O&M contracts (ONGC, consortium with Supreme Hydro)
segments.commentary: Samudra Sevak and Samudra Prabha contracts run to 31 March 2028 with values of Rs348 crore and Rs270 crore; Supreme Hydro holds about 10%. Billing is monthly. Samudra Prabha expected to start work around the first week of June 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue and bottom-line growth of about 15%, per Sunil Gupta; management declined to go beyond 15%.
EBITDA margin guided to a stable 40-42%; quarterly margins may vary by 2-3 points with dry dock and contract mix.
Seamec Paladin not operating in Q4 or April-May; revenue expected from June only if geopolitical situation clears.
SEAMEC-II contracted only till August 2026, then a small dry dock; SEAMEC AGASTYA gives full-year revenue in FY27.
SEAMEC ANANT deployment expected in about one more quarter; acquisition funding source depends on the transaction.
capex_capacity: FY27 scheduled capex for SEAMEC ANANT about $70 million.
Three owned vessels due for dry dock in FY27 monsoon season, plus two ONGC O&M vessels.
SEAMEC AGASTYA integrated and operating, on ONGC charter.
Management says it is not chasing fleet growth aggressively given high capex; one bulk carrier (Pearl or Gallant) may be sold in FY27, subject to market conditions.
demand_pricing: Management says market is buoyant and rates may rise for another couple of years, but the DSV market is balanced with no new competitors.
Competition persists in bidding; management denied pricing pressure in bids currently.
Pricing: ONGC charter rates benchmarked against international rates; EPC/spot work priced on client's internal estimate.
Middle East demand expected to rise once the conflict settles, per management.
Price competition and foreign entry barriers were described as limited by protectionism and entry barriers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the O&M revenue from Supreme Hydro consortium 90% for Seamec, and how is it billed?
qa_highlights.answer: Supreme Hydro holds about 10% and provides technical know-how, manuals and personnel; billing is monthly to ONGC at month end.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 incremental revenue be about Rs500 crore from AGASTYA, SWORDFISH, ANANT and O&M contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the assumption was not right and would not go beyond 15% guidance, citing Paladin being idle and SEAMEC-II contracted only till August 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What were FY26 capex and FY27 plans?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 capex was about Rs300 crore; FY27 scheduled capex is about $70 million for ANANT.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 margin one-off or should margins be lower?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-off in Q4; Paladin idle for Q4 and April-May; margin guided stable at 40-42%, with 1-2% upside possible depending on utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Diamond's rate far below spot OSV rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Ocean and Emerald are larger vessels doing geotech and stimulation work, so comparison is not like-for-like; Diamond is an OSV, an aberration in a DSV-focused fleet.

qa_highlights.question: Is there impairment on UK subsidiary and any progress there?
qa_highlights.answer: Impairment taken on prudence due to geopolitics, not abandonment; no accounting or execution impact; no new contract announced yet.

risks_watch: Seamec Paladin stuck in Dubai dry dock until Strait of Hormuz reopens; April-May revenue lost and June uncertain.
Vessel SEAMEC-II contract ends August 2026, followed by dry dock and possible spot-market exposure.
ANANT deployment delay of about one quarter; ONGC may not permit movement during field operations.
Off-hire days are unpaid; dry dock schedule and monsoon season may dent utilisation.
Rupee appreciation and escalation of the West Asia conflict flagged as risks to the Saudi Aramco vessel.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 and the demand outlook, but cautious and evasive on FY27 specifics: it declined to quantify beyond 15% growth and repeatedly deferred on the timing of contracts, ANANT and the UK subsidiary, citing geopolitical uncertainty.
key_quotes: I am proud to report Seamec's highest-ever annual revenue and profitability in Financial Year '26, which is achieved through strong operational execution, higher fleet deployment, improved vessel utilization, and disciplined project delivery across domestic and international markets.
Sir, your assumption is not right and I would not like to comment further beyond 15%.
We have not abandoned anything. The only thing is because of the current geopolitical situation, on a prudence basis, we have just taken that impairment.
When the vessel is on off-hire, company is not being paid for those off-hire days.
